# reco_custom_dashboard (Resource)

Manages a Reco custom dashboard. The Reco API cannot delete dashboards, so destroying this resource only removes it from Terraform state; the dashboard remains in Reco and must be deleted in the Reco UI.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "reco_custom_dashboard" "security_overview" {
  name        = "Security Overview"
  visibility  = "DASHBOARD_VISIBILITY_SHARED_READ"
  folder_path = "/team/security"

  # A dashboard has sections, each with cells, each holding widgets.
  # Widget keys are listed by GET /api/v1/external-api/dashboards/widgets.
  spec = jsonencode({
    sections = [{
      columns = 2
      cells = [{
        colSpan = 1
        widgets = [{ widget = "DASHBOARD_WIDGET_TOTAL_SAAS_APPS" }]
      }]
    }]
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name (1-200 characters).
- `spec` (String) Dashboard layout as a JSON object string, for example from jsonencode(). It must contain a `sections` array whose entries hold a `cells` array of `widgets` (`{"widget": "<key>"}`); valid widget keys are listed by the Reco API endpoint GET /api/v1/external-api/dashboards/widgets. Reco rewrites SCIM filter shorthand (`{"scim": "..."}`) into structured filters when saving, so use structured filters to avoid a permanent diff.

### Optional

- `folder_path` (String) Folder path of the dashboard, e.g. "/" or "/team/security". Defaults to "/".
- `visibility` (String) Who can see the dashboard: DASHBOARD_VISIBILITY_PRIVATE, DASHBOARD_VISIBILITY_SHARED_READ, or DASHBOARD_VISIBILITY_SHARED_WRITE. Defaults to private.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the dashboard was created (read-only).
- `created_by` (String) Email of the dashboard owner (read-only).
- `created_by_name` (String) Display name of the dashboard owner (read-only).
- `id` (String) Dashboard ID (set after create).
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp when the dashboard was last updated (read-only).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = reco_custom_dashboard.security_overview
  id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
}
```
